newsitem.title: USA: Westchester Cty, N.Y. to get $40 mln for watershed.
newsitem.headline: Westchester Cty, N.Y. to get $40 mln for watershed.

text.p: Westchester County, N.Y., on Monday will get almost $40 million from New York City under the pact the city reached with Albany and upstate areas to protect its watershed, a county spokesman said Friday.
The payment will be the first one the city will make under the watershed agreement, said Geoff Ryan, a spokesman for the New York City Department of Environmental Protection.

He added that Putnam County, the Catskill Watershed Corp, and the Coalition of Watershed Towns, a group of towns and counties west of the Hudson River that are part of the city's watershed system, also will get checks from the city that day but declined to say how much.

Jim Doughty, Westchester's spokesman, said that the county's East of Hudson Water Quality Investment Program will get about $38 million, for projects like sewer upgrades, while Good Neighbor projects that aim to help offset the costs of protecting New York City's water system will get around $1.6 million.

The watershed agreement, which was designed to help the city avoid spending billions of dollars on a sewage filtration plant, calls for it to spend $260 million to buy land around its reservoirs and $334 million in new programs with local communities, among other expenses.
The New York City comptroller, Alan Hevesi, has estimated the agreement could cost the city about $2.2 billion.
